name: admin.apps.approve
tokens: Live-tested 2026-09-20 with app_id, request_id, team_id, and enterprise_id in various combinations, both team- and enterprise-scoped xoxc: every combination returned either team_not_found or not_an_admin, never ok:true. not_an_admin is the interesting one -- a plain statement that this account, despite an Organization-level authenticated CLI session, is not an actual admin for this governance action. Contrast with admin.apps.uninstall, which succeeded for the same account. See methods/admin-write-scope-2026-09.md.
purpose: Approve an app for installation on a workspace.

allow_child_auto_install.desc: Auto-create an Admin-Approved App automation rule that pre-approves future child app installs from this manager app.

app_id.desc: The id of the app to approve.

request_id.desc: The id of the request to approve.

team_id.desc: The ID of the workspace to approve the app on.

enterprise_id.desc: The ID of the enterprise to approve the app on.

user_scopes.desc: User scopes to approve for the app.

bot_scopes.desc: Bot scopes to approve for the app.

safety_note_for_agents: This catalog documents Slack's UNDOCUMENTED/internal API surface for a specific workspace (Hack Club, Enterprise Grid). Calling an undocumented method with params_known=false means you would be guessing params against a real backend with unknown side effects -- do not do this against a real account/token without a human in the loop, and never call anything shaped like a write (*.delete, *.set, *.remove, *.create, *.update, and similar) without explicit human confirmation and a clear understanding of the blast radius, even when params_known=true. 'existence-only' verified does NOT mean 'safe to call' -- it only means the method name is real.
